place_fields.vibe: Historic coastal fort amid lush greenery and moats, suited to heritage walks and photography.
place_fields.summary: Mirjan Fort is a historic laterite fort near Gokarna in coastal Karnataka, with ramparts, bastions, gateways and a moat in a lush setting.
place_fields.best_time: The official Karnataka Tourism page recommends avoiding heavy monsoon rain; its page also describes monsoon greenery, so drier weather is the safer practical choice for walking the fort.

planning_attributes.description: A 16th-century coastal fortress near Gokarna, associated with the Nawayath Sultanate and later Queen Chennabhairadevi; it retains ramparts, bastions, gateways and a moat.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Karnataka Tourism identifies Mirjan Fort with Queen Chennabhairadevi, the Pepper Queen, while its Gokarna destination page describes the fort as a 16th-century laterite fortress built by the Nawayath Sultanate and later controlled by Chennabhairadevi.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Karnataka Tourism places the fort about 21–22 km north of Gokarna with road access from Karwar and Kumta; the nearest railway station is Kumta, about 12 km away, with autos and taxis available locally.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Karnataka Tourism states the fort is open 9 AM to 5 PM and entry is free; it advises avoiding visits during heavy monsoon rains.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Use caution on slippery paths, especially in wet weather; carry water and sun protection and avoid heavy monsoon conditions.
planning_attributes.notes: Karnataka Tourism also describes four main gates, underground passages, water wells, bastions and riverbank surroundings.
